commits.author: ravwojdyla-agent
commits.message:
[taskforge] Make GlmClient picklable and usable in each event loop (#10396)

A pickled `GlmClient` now holds only its endpoint source and provider
config, so code can send a client to Zephyr workers, and each copy opens
its own connections there. Before, `pickle.dumps(GlmClient(...))` raised
`TypeError: cannot pickle '_thread.RLock' object`, because the httpx
pool holds locks.

The client also opens one httpx pool for each event loop that uses it,
and it drops the pools of closed loops. A Zephyr function is
synchronous, so it starts each model call with `asyncio.run`, and an
httpx pool from a closed loop fails on its next kept-alive connection
with `RuntimeError: Event loop is closed`. `__aexit__` closes the pool
of the running loop, and each loop's SDK client moves to a new endpoint
at its next request, as before.

With this change, the failed-run analysis of #10265 can take a
`ModelClient` and drop its client factory. The two new tests fail on
main: one at the pickle, and one with "Event loop is closed" on a
kept-alive connection.

commits.author: ravwojdyla-agent
commits.message:
rolloutengine: let a shell harness set the output limit of each command (#10442)

Add `ShellHarness.output_limit_bytes` to limit the stdout and stderr
returned to the model by each shell command. The default remains
`DEFAULT_MACHINE_OUTPUT_LIMIT_BYTES` (1 MiB), preserving the training
harness truncation chosen in #10184. A harness that runs an agent for
its results can set a lower limit.

One MiB of text is about 250,000 tokens, roughly the full GLM context
window. In a 30-idea run of agentic Taskforge, a build program printed
an entire TaskSpec. The next request overflowed the context window and
ended the session.

The harness refuses an `output_limit_bytes` of 0 or less, because
ShellSim slices a stream with a negative limit and returns almost all of
it. `docs/references/task-rollouts.md` documents the parameter and its
default.

This branch also holds #10443, which merged into it: `CapabilityIdea`,
`capability_idea_record` and `FILE_SAFE_ID` move from
`experiments/post_training/capability_driven_envs/catalog.py` to
`taskforge.capability`, so that a generator in the library can take an
idea as input. The behavior does not change.

Part of #10152.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[SkyRL] Share BF16 checkpoint records with FP32 master weights (#10437)

Deduplicate BF16 model weights against their synchronized FP32 optimizer
masters in Megatron S3 checkpoints. Both logical names reference one
stored FP32 record. Full training restores load masters and moments
once, then cast masters into BF16 model buffers and synchronize
distributed parameter shards. Model-only restores read the shared
records and cast them to BF16.

Buffers and weights without matching model-space masters retain separate
records. For matching BF16 parameters with FP32 masters and Adam
moments, tensor storage and full-restore reads fall from 14 to 12 bytes
per parameter: about 14%, or 134 GB for a 939 GB checkpoint with this
layout. Model-only loads read FP32 records, twice the weight bytes of a
BF16-only copy.

commits.author: asartran
commits.message:
[dependencies] Bump certifi to 2026.10.19 (#10435)

Bump certifi from 2026.1.4 to 2026.10.19 so marin environments stop
trusting the compromised eMudhra root.

On 2026-10-17, private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate CAs under the
`emSign ECC Root CA - G3` root were found to be recoverable from their
public certificates
([CVE-2026-111943](https://access.redhat.com/security/vulnerabilities/RHSB-2026-012),
[Mozilla/Google/Apple
response](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/mozilla-google-apple-block-compromised-emudhra-ca-certificates/)).
Mozilla distrusted that root, and certifi 2026.10.19 removes it from the
CA bundle. Python HTTPS clients that use certifi (requests, httpx, pip,
huggingface_hub) ignore the OS trust store, so OS `ca-certificates`
updates do not protect them. Until the lock changes, every `uv sync`
reinstalls the old bundle.

The new bundle also carries nine months of routine Mozilla root-store
changes: 20 other roots removed (including the legacy DigiCert Global,
Assured ID, and High Assurance EV roots) and 5 added.

The lock was regenerated with uv 0.13.1 so the diff covers only the
certifi entry. uv 0.13.2 and later also rewrite about 600 platform
marker lines.

commits.author: ravwojdyla-agent
commits.message:
[taskforge] Turn failed rollouts into capability ideas (#10265)

Doc:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1DXtl3bOsGvhb1usA3cfZ6-G1TDyObf_G0g-TRVq4DtA

Turn policy failures into capability ideas that `task_workpieces` and
`generate_tasks` can use to create training tasks.
`analyze_failed_runs(rollouts, make_client, *, pass_threshold,
max_new_ideas, shard_size, extract_ideas_llm_policy,
merge_ideas_llm_policy, catalog_version, min_tasks_per_idea=2,
max_ideas_per_merge=1000)` takes `(TaskSpec, GradedRollout)` pairs and
returns the plan of one Zephyr map-reduce pipeline, as the doc proposes.
The source is the rollouts in shards of `shard_size`. `filter` keeps the
policy failures, `flat_map(yield_ideas)` makes one structured call for
each failed rollout, `reduce(merge_ideas, merge_idea_lists)` merges each
shard and then the lists of the shards, with one structured call for at
most `max_ideas_per_merge` ideas, and `flat_map(to_ideas)` makes the
`CapabilityIdea` values, the ideas with more rollouts first.

Each capability is a general skill that transfers to many tasks and
domains, such as the answer format, tool use, a stop to loops of
repeated calls, or a careful reading of the task. It holds the catalog
fields `name`, `outcome`, `includes`, and `excludes`, and it does not
describe the failed tasks, so `generate_tasks` writes the details of the
training tasks. A rollout that stopped at its turn limit counts as a gap
only if it used its turns on repeated or unneeded steps, because the
policy does not see the limit.

`policy_failed` is true for a grade below `pass_threshold`, an invalid
submission, or an attempt that ran past its deadline or whose harness
failed after a model turn, because a slow or looping policy or a bad
tool call can cause those. It is false for task, grader, and
infrastructure failures and for interruptions by the model server or the
machine, so those do not become training targets. The rollout's first
line names the operation that interrupted it. The call for a rollout
gives up to three ideas, or none if the rollout shows no gap. It sees a
summary line, the tools that the task gave, and the messages, with no
grader or its answer. The task comes with each rollout because the
record does not keep the tools. A rollout whose reply stays invalid
gives no ideas and adds 1 to the pipeline counter
`failed_runs.invalid_replies`.

A `MaybeIdea` keeps its evidence as a set of run IDs, and the IDs of
their tasks. A merge call sees each idea with its number of rollouts and
gives the line IDs that each merged idea holds, and code takes the union
of their evidence, so a rollout counts once. The reply must name only
its lines and give each merged idea a different ID, and the structured
call sends an invalid reply back with the error. A reply can leave out
the lines of rare skills, as the prompt keeps the ideas that explain the
most rollouts, and the pipeline counter `failed_runs.dropped_rollouts`
adds the rollouts that the merged ideas no longer cite. A rule that put
each line in exactly one merged idea failed 2 of 3 merges of the 797
tau-bench failures and made larger catch-all ideas, and the merge that
can leave out lines lost the evidence of at most 2.2% of the rollouts.
The same merge serves the two levels, and one group needs no second
merge. The merge reply lists the line IDs of each merged idea, and GLM
sometimes runs away to the output limit in a long structured reply, so a
merge makes up to three calls. A merged idea cannot repeat its line IDs
as its `includes`, because GLM wrote the IDs there for every capability
in 6 of 27 merges. A final idea must cite failed rollouts of at least
`min_tasks_per_idea` tasks, or of every failed task when there are
fewer, so that one defective grader on a task with many samples cannot
make an idea by itself. The merges rank such ideas last, so that they do
not take the place of an idea that cites enough tasks. A merge call sees
at most `max_ideas_per_merge` ideas, about 66 prompt tokens each, and
more ideas merge in rounds, so neither a large shard nor many shards can
make a merge prompt too long. The calls of one shard run one after
another on one worker, and the shards run in parallel. Zephyr calls the
functions on its workers, outside an event loop, so each call makes its
own client with `make_client`, for example `functools.partial(GlmClient,
source, GLM_PROVIDER)`.

This design replaces a managed agent that read the failed rollouts as
files on a ShellSim machine. Both designs ran with GLM-5.3 at low
reasoning effort on real failed rollouts: tau-bench trajectories of
GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet (72, 144, and all 797 failures) and 120
SWE-agent rollouts on GitHub issues. The agent's evidence named 16%, 6%,
and 1% of the tau-bench failures and 8% of the SWE failures. Per-rollout
calls read every rollout. They beat the agent in every direct comparison
on these sets, with a GLM judge, and with a Claude judge on all sets
except the 797 failures. They also found all the failure categories of a
reference taxonomy. The merged capabilities are broader than the
agent's: a blind judge rated their focus about 3 of 5, against about 4.4
for the agent. A merge that kept more and narrower capabilities lost
recall. Results:
`s3://marin-us-east-02a/user/rav/projects/analyze-failed-runs/compare/`.

This pipeline ran end to end with GLM-5.3 on cw-us-east-02a, with a
local Zephyr client (Iris jobs `/rav/zephyr-batch-a` and
`/rav/zephyr-batch-b`). On 72 tau-bench failures in one shard it gave 8
ideas in 279 s, and on 144 failures in two shards of 72 it gave 7 ideas
in 320 s. Both cited every failed rollout and skipped none. An earlier
version with one shard for each rollout and a `reshard` before the merge
took 37 s and 57 s on the same sets and found every category of the
reference taxonomy, because its per-rollout calls ran in parallel.

`FILE_SAFE_ID` moves from `generate_tasks` to `catalog.py`, so that the
analysis does not import the generation driver. `marin-taskforge`
depends on `marin-rolloutengine` for the rollout records and the task
tools and on `marin-zephyr` for the pipeline, and `taskforge-unit` also
runs when `lib/rolloutengine`, `lib/zephyr`, or `lib/fray` changes.

[shellbox] Prebuild snapshots and retry rejected Daytona creates (#10332)

Expose snapshot preparation without creating a sandbox. Reuse the
existing image-source/resource identity, or accept an explicit snapshot
name for launcher-owned mappings. Registry references must be
digest-pinned for immutable snapshot reuse.

Retry Daytona sandbox-creation HTTP 429 responses within the caller's
startup deadline. Retry only when the SDK traceback identifies the
rejected create request; a failure during a later read must not create a
second sandbox. Respect the provider retry delay and preserve
cancellation.

commits.message:
[docs] Require responsible-use text on Hugging Face model cards (#10337)

The Hugging Face model upload instructions now require the model
repository's root `README.md` to include this exact paragraph on every
upload or update:

> We release our tools to the public with the intent that they are used
safely, ethically, and responsibly. They are meant to contribute to the
public's understanding of science, and aid in its advancement. By using
this Marin model, you agree to comply with all applicable law.

The paragraph accompanies the existing research-artifact warning and
OpenMDW 1.1 license requirements. The instructions prohibit duplicate
copies of either paragraph and require post-upload checks of the
published `README.md` and `LICENSE` for the warning, responsible-use
paragraph, OpenMDW 1.1 license metadata, and full license text.
